page.layout: One printed page: one column of running text, with three marginal notes in the right margin. Running head at top, page number at top right. Signature and catchword at the foot. The strip at the left edge is the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: Apollo, ego Cephæ, sic apud nos istiusmodi voces audiantur, ego sum Lutheri, ego Calvini, ego Arminii, ego Socini. Quin esto {1}Rom. 3 4. omnis homo mendax, & verax solus Deus. Non est dignus qui sit Christi, qui non est unius Christi discipulus. Actum est de fidei Christianæ simplicitate & sinceritate, postquam itum est in partes: Neque ulla spes est ante restitutum iri pristino vigori & virori Religionem Christi, quàm diducta tot fracturis & sciffuris vulnera, fraternæ condescensionis oleo velut malægmate delinita, in eandem Fidei & Charitatis unitatem coëant & coalescant.

XXX. Cavendum porrò Tertiò, ne pravis affectibus indulgentes, ita nos abduci patiamur in cujusquam personæ admirationem, ut ex ipsius authoritate toti pendeamus, {2}Jud. v. 16.Θαυμάζοντες ὠφελείας χάριν[?]. Quibus verbis intendit digitum Apostolus ad ipsissimum totius mali fontem. Nempe non aliunde emanavit omnis illa omnium[?] perversa admiratio quam ex perdita illa & nimia sua admiratione. Dum quisque propriæ utilitati studet, infervit honori, gloriæ velificatur; alios omnes æstimat ex suo commodo: & corrupto jam hisce affectibus judicio, eos protinus admiratur maximè, quos utilitati, honori, gloriæ, aliisque suis cupiditatibus minimè adversaturos arbitratur.
Quod ipsum alter etiam Apostolus, quem ante citavimus clare significat, ubi notat homines sibi {3}2 Tim. 4.3.κατὰ τὰς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας praeceptores de-ligere.

XXXI. Cæterùm ut, non obstantibus quæ à me dicta sunt, sua constet interim & Ecclesiæ Catholicæ, & unicuique viro docto & pio, justa authoritas: Admonendi estis primò, judicio & piæ Universalis Ecclesiæ, in sacrarum literarum interpretatione, & in dijudicandis fidei & mo-

page.notes: Doubtful readings: the Greek in the second and third notes (after {2} and {3}) is faint and only partly legible; the letters marked [?] are best readings. "omnium" after "illa" is partly obscured and marked [?]. The initial "A" of "Apollo" is damaged. The running head "Præleƈtio" uses the ct ligature, written here as ct. The catchword "rum" is the start of the next page's first word, continuing the hyphenated "mo-". Marginal references are transcribed as printed. The left edge strip shows part of the neighbouring page and is excluded.
